title: Lesson 1: Square Root by Inspection — Vedic Digit-Grouping
subtopics: Units digit patterns for perfect squares
Tens digit from the first group
MCQ: identify digits of the square root
learningGoals: Group digits of a perfect square right-to-left in pairs to determine the number of digits in its square root.
Use units digit patterns to identify the units digit of a square root instantly.
Determine the tens digit by estimating from the first group of digits.
Find square roots of 4-digit and 6-digit perfect squares by inspection.
coreIdeas: Group the digits right-to-left in pairs; the number of groups gives the number of digits in the square root.
The units digit of a perfect square uniquely narrows the units digit of its root to two possibilities.
The tens digit comes from the largest integer whose square is less than or equal to the first group.
This method replaces long-division square root with two fast inspections — board exam level speed.

workedExamples.method: Group right-to-left: 7 | 84. First group 7 → tens digit: 2 (since 2²=4≤7<9=3²). Units digit: 84 ends in 4, so root ends in 2 or 8. Try 28: 28²=784. Answer: 28.
Group: 15 | 21. First group 15 → tens digit: 3 (3²=9≤15<16=4²). Units digit: 21 ends in 1, so root ends in 1 or 9. Try 39: 39²=1521. Answer: 39.
Group: 53 | 29. First group 53 → tens digit: 7 (7²=49≤53<64=8²). Units digit: 29 ends in 9, so root ends in 3 or 7. Try 73: 73²=5329. Answer: 73.
Group: 98 | 01. First group 98 → tens digit: 9 (9²=81≤98<100=10²). Units digit: 01 ends in 1, so root ends in 1 or 9. Try 99: 99²=9801. Answer: 99.

starterPractice: Warm-up: Group 625 right-to-left. How many groups do you get?
Guided: For √1024, what does the first group tell you about the tens digit?
Independent: Find √2916 using the digit-grouping method.

sessionFlow.subtopic: Units digit patterns for perfect squares
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise B: The units digit table
sessionFlow.coachHook: This is the board-exam shortcut everyone misses! The units digit of a perfect square tells you exactly which units digit the root can have. Memorise this table and you have cut the work in half.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Units digit table: square ends 1 → root ends 1 or 9; ends 4 → root ends 2 or 8; ends 9 → root ends 3 or 7; ends 6 → root ends 4 or 6; ends 5 → root ends 5; ends 0 → root ends 0.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: If a perfect square ends in 6, what can the root end in?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: A perfect square ends in 9. What are the two possible units digits of its root?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: √___ ends in 4 or 6 — what digit does the original square end in?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: You have cracked the units digit code! This alone eliminates half the options in any MCQ.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: If the square ends in 9, the root ends in 3 or 7 (because 3²=9 and 7²=49).
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick test: what units digit does a root have if the square ends in 1? In 4?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise C: Nailing the tens digit
sessionFlow.coachHook: You know the units digit — now get the tens digit in one step! Find the largest integer whose square does not exceed the first group. That is your tens digit. This is board-exam level analysis.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: √1764: group 17|64. First group 17. Largest n with n²≤17: 4²=16≤17, 5²=25>17. So tens digit=4. Units digit of 1764 is 4 → root ends 2 or 8. Check 42: 42²=1764. Answer: 42.

sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: For first group 29: 5²=25≤29 but 6²=36>29. So the tens digit is 5.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Practice: find the tens digit for first groups 7, 15, 42, 63.
